Alderbury and West Grimstead Church of England Primary School
"Foundations for Life"
🌟 Looking for a nurturing village primary school? Join us for our Open Morning on 18th November 2026. Email admin@alderbury.wilts.sch.uk to reserve your place.
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Alderbury & West Grimstead Church of England Primary School, part of the Pickwick Academy Trust. It is a pleasure to introduce you to our happy, caring and ambitious school community.
At AWGS, we believe that every child is unique, valued and capable of achieving great things. Our Christian vision, Foundations for Life, underpins all that we do, helping children to flourish academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually. We nurture curiosity, encourage kindness and respect and inspire children to become confident learners and responsible citizens.
We are proud of the warm relationships that sit at the heart of our school. Our dedicated staff team works hard to create a calm, welcoming environment where children feel safe, supported and ready to learn. Through a rich curriculum, high expectations and a genuine commitment to every child, we strive to ensure all pupils achieve their very best.
Whether you are considering AWGS for your child or would simply like to learn more about our school, we would be delighted to welcome you. We encourage prospective families to visit, meet our children and staff, and experience first-hand what makes our village school such a special place to learn and grow.
To arrange a visit, please contact us at admin@alderbury.wilts.sch.uk.
We look forward to meeting you.
Mrs E. Woolf - Headteacher

If you are interested in applying for a place at the school mid-year, please contact the school office on admin@alderbury.wilts.sch.uk in the first instance and we will be happy to discuss this with you.

pageCache.pageTitle: Alderbury and West Grimstead Church of England Primary School - Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
Our Vision
At Alderbury & West Grimstead Church of England Primary School, our vision is to provide Foundations for Life, rooted in Christian faith and values, so that every child can flourish.
Our vision is based on the parable of the wise and foolish builders, told by Jesus (Matthew 7:24-27). As a school, we aim to support all of our children in laying good foundations for their lives, especially in the following 4 areas:
​Learning – We encourage our pupils to be independent, reflective, resourceful, responsive and resilient.
​Individuals – We encourage our pupils to have freedom of thought and speech, showing respect for themselves and others.
​Friendship – We encourage our pupils to form a strong and cohesive community, developing positive relationships in school and beyond.
​Environment – We encourage our pupils to take responsibility for the environment and to look after the earth’s resources.
Guided by the teachings of Jesus, we seek to nurture the whole child — academically, socially, emotionally and spiritually. We are committed to creating a loving, inclusive community where everyone is valued as unique and made in the image of God. Through high expectations, meaningful learning and strong relationships, we enable our children to grow in wisdom, confidence and compassion, prepared for life in all its fullness.
Our vision shapes every aspect of school life, ensuring that children are supported to become thoughtful, responsible citizens who contribute positively to their communities and the wider world.
Our Christian Values
Our Christian values are at the heart of daily life at Alderbury & West Grimstead Church of England Primary School. They shape our relationships, guide our behaviour and help our children understand how to live well together, following the example of Jesus.
“I am friendly and caring in my words and actions.”
Kindness is central to how we treat one another at AWGS. Children are encouraged to show compassion, empathy and care in all that they say and do, creating a nurturing and supportive community where everyone feels valued and safe. Through kindness, pupils learn the importance of forgiveness, service and looking after others.
You must clothe yourselves with compassion and kindness. Colossians 3:12
✝ Justice
“I am fair in how I treat other people and stand up for justice whenever I can.”
Justice guides our understanding of fairness, honesty and responsibility. We support children to recognise right from wrong, to treat others equitably and to speak up for those who may need support. Through this value, pupils develop a strong moral compass and an awareness of their role in making a positive difference in the world.
The Lord has told us what is good. What he requires of us is this: to do what is just, to be loving and to live in humble fellowship with our God. Micah 6:8
✝ Respect
“I treat others how I would like to be treated.”
Respect underpins all relationships within our school community. Children learn to value themselves and others, to listen carefully, celebrate diversity and show consideration in their actions and choices. Respect enables our community to live and learn together in harmony.
Love your neighbour as you love yourself. Matthew 22:39
At AWGS, our vision and values ensure that every child is known, valued and loved and supported to flourish as they grow into confident, compassionate individuals with strong foundations for life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Alderbury and West Grimstead Church of England Primary School - Church Schools Flourishing
pageCache.text:
Church Schools Flourishing
As a Church of England school, our Christian vision of Foundations for Life and our core values of Kindness, Justice and Respect shape every aspect of school life. Through these values, we strive to enable all pupils and adults to flourish in body, mind and spirit — becoming confident, compassionate and curious individuals who contribute positively to our community and beyond.
Collective Worship
Collective worship is a central part of our daily life and a key expression of our church school identity. It brings children and staff together regularly to pray, reflect, praise and explore Christian teaching. While daily worship is a statutory requirement for all schools, for us it is so much more — it is a special time when we grow together spiritually, celebrate our values and deepen our understanding of God’s love.
Our acts of worship:
Are Christian in character, rooted in Bible teaching and the traditions of the Church of England.
Include leadership from school staff, pupils, local clergy and church volunteers.
Provide regular opportunities for reflection, prayer and response to the Christian message.
Celebrate key moments in the Christian calendar and link to our school values.
Children are actively involved in planning and leading worship, which enhances its impact and enables them to take ownership of their spiritual development.
Collective Worships which take place are:
Monday - ‘Values’ Worship led by Headteacher
Tuesday - News Day Tuesday led by pupils
Wednesday - Worship led by Rev Marcia/Local Church Leaders
Thursday - Celebration!
Living Our Vision and Values
Our Christian vision and values do not sit separately from daily school life — they are lived out in everything we do. In school, pupils are encouraged to:
Show Kindness in their words and actions, caring for others as part of a loving community.
Act Justly, treating others fairly and speaking up for what is right.
Demonstrate Respect in how they treat others and the world around them.
These values shape positive behaviour, supportive relationships and an environment in which everyone can feel safe, valued and included.
Across the curriculum, through day-to-day interactions, and in times of worship, pupils reflect on how these values connect to their own lives and to Christian teaching.
Spiritual Development and Flourishing
At AWGS, flourishing means much more than academic success. We seek to nurture the whole child — intellectually, emotionally and spiritually — enabling pupils to explore life’s big questions, reflect on their experiences and make meaning in the world around them. Spiritual development is encouraged through:
Times for reflection and prayer
Opportunities to explore personal beliefs and values
Engagement with Bible stories and Christian teaching
Collective worship, RE and class discussions
Our school community values respectful dialogue, encouraging pupils to express their own views and to listen with openness to others.
Church and Community Links
We are fortunate to have strong relationships with our local church leaders and congregations, who visit school to lead worship and enrich our Christian life. These links help to strengthen the Christian character of the school and provide meaningful connections between school, church and community.
Our SIAMS Context
In our most recent SIAMS inspection, AWGS was recognised as a highly successful church school with strong Christian leadership and a nurturing culture where every member of the community is treated in line with our values of Kindness, Justice and Respect. Pupils were described as confident ambassadors for the school, demonstrating how the vision is lived out in daily life.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to AWGS
A very warm welcome to Alderbury & West Grimstead Church of England Primary School and thank you for visiting our website.
We are proud to be a small, caring and inclusive village school, nestled in the heart of Alderbury near Salisbury in Wiltshire. With just five classes, we have a wonderful family feel, where every child is known, valued and supported. We welcome children aged 4 to 11 from our local community and surrounding areas, creating a close-knit school where children, families and staff work together.
At AWGS, our Christian values are at the heart of everything we do. We believe education is a shared journey, built on strong relationships, kindness and a sense of belonging. Guided by our vision of Foundations for Life, we give every child the confidence, encouragement and opportunities they need to grow into happy, compassionate and curious learners.
Our curriculum is rich, creative and engaging, inspiring children to ask big questions, explore new ideas and develop a lifelong love of learning. Across all subjects, pupils are encouraged to think independently, solve problems, express themselves creatively and aim high. Through memorable and meaningful experiences, we help children develop the knowledge, skills and personal qualities they need to flourish both now and in the future.
Being a small village school means that our community is at the heart of school life. We celebrate our individual strengths while supporting one another and our pupils benefit from strong relationships across the whole school. Our family feel extends beyond the classroom, with children, parents, staff and the wider community working together to make AWGS a special place to learn and grow.
We are proud to be part of the Pickwick Academy Trust, working collaboratively with other schools to strengthen our educational offer and support our pupils’ wellbeing, development and achievement.
We warmly invite you to come and experience our wonderful school for yourself. A visit is the best way to discover the welcoming atmosphere, family feel and strong sense of community that make AWGS so special. Please contact the school office on 01722 710464 or admin@alderbury.wilts.sch.uk to arrange a private tour with me.

Artist
Art & Design at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
At AWGS, we believe that being an Artist is about far more than producing artwork — it is about exploring ideas, expressing emotions, developing creativity and learning to see the world in new ways. Art is a powerful tool for thinking, communicating and understanding and we want every child to feel inspired, confident and capable as an Artist.
Being Inspired Through Art
Each year group has at least one enquiry where being an Artist is the lead state of being. In these enquiries, pupils explore artistic techniques, study the work of influential artists and develop their own creative responses.
Throughout the year, many other enquiries include being an Artist as a secondary state, meaning that children may be Scientists, Historians or Designers while using art to express, represent or deepen their learning. This helps pupils understand that art is not separate from other subjects — it is a powerful way to communicate ideas across the curriculum.
What We Aim to Develop
Through our Art & Design curriculum, we encourage pupils to:
Explore and experiment with a wide range of materials and techniques
Develop their creativity, imagination and personal expression
Build confidence in drawing, painting, sculpture and mixed media
Study and appreciate the work of artists, designers and craftspeople
Reflect on their work and the work of others
Use art to communicate ideas, emotions and understanding
Make meaningful links between art and the wider world
Additional Opportunities
Beyond planned enquiries, pupils are encouraged to take part in additional artistic experiences throughout the year. These may include:
Whole‑school art projects
Gallery events and exhibitions
Outdoor art and nature‑based creativity
Community art initiatives

pageCache.pageTitle: Alderbury and West Grimstead Church of England Primary School - Wraparound Care
pageCache.text:
Wraparound Care
At Alderbury & West Grimstead Church of England Primary School, we understand that family life doesn’t always fit neatly around the school day. That’s why we offer friendly, flexible and reliable wraparound care to give parents and carers peace of mind, while ensuring children have a happy and positive start and finish to their day.
Whether you need an early start or a little extra time after school, our Breakfast Club and After School Club provide welcoming, engaging environments where children can relax, play and enjoy time with friends.
🌅 Breakfast Club — Start the Day Right
From 7:30am | School Hall | Drop-off via the main school entrance
Give your child a relaxed and enjoyable start to the school day with our Breakfast Club.
Children can enjoy a variety of breakfast options, spend time with friends, take part in fun activities and settle into their day with the support of familiar members of our school team.
Our Breakfast Club is run by Mrs Telfer and Mrs Soul and is open to all pupils.
Good news — we currently have spaces available! Bookings can be made easily through Arbor.
For prices, availability or further information, please contact: 📧 admin@alderbury.wilts.sch.uk
🎨 After School Club — More Time to Play
End of the school day – 5:30pm | Alderbury Pre-School
Need a little more flexibility at the end of the school day? Our After School Club, hosted by Alderbury Pre-School, provides a warm, nurturing space where children can continue to learn, play and have fun after lessons finish.
Working closely with Alderbury Pre-School means we can provide a smooth transition from school to after-school care, helping children feel comfortable and settled.
At the end of the school day, school staff walk children to Alderbury Pre-School, located next door, where they are cared for until collection.
Sessions are booked directly with Alderbury Pre-School.
For bookings, prices and availability, please contact: 📧 alderburypreschool@gmail.com
🌐 Alderbury Pre-School Parent Information
🎨 Creative and imaginative activities
🧸 Play-based learning and time with friends
🌳 Outdoor play and activities
💛 A welcoming, nurturing environment
💛 Quality Care, Right on Your Doorstep
From 7:30am through to 5:30pm, our wraparound provision is designed to make family life that little bit easier — while ensuring children are happy, cared for and having fun beyond the classroom.

Author
English at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
Being an Author (as both a reader and a writer) at AWGS is an integral part of all that we do and involves an engaging, text-based approach to teaching and learning. In all year groups, children are immersed in high quality texts, promoting a love of both reading and writing and developing associated skills as part of a well-planned, progressive curriculum. Engaging books provide the drivers for our writing learning journeys, with children writing for a range of genres, audiences and purposes. Dedicated reading sessions are focused on the teaching of specific reading skills, developing fluency and comprehension appropriate for pupils’ age and stage. Children’s reading and writing learning experiences are linked and mutually supportive. Wherever possible, these also support teaching and learning in other curriculum subjects, with opportunities for pupils to understand the real-life contexts for reading and writing.
We encourage all children to use a neat, accurate and joined style of handwriting and you can access resources to support this from home here.

pageCache.text:
Engineer
Design & Technology at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
Being an Engineer at AWGS gives pupils the opportunity to design, create and innovate. Through purposeful, practical activities, children learn how to take risks, solve problems and develop their creativity. Skills are taught progressively as pupils move through the school, enabling them to build confidence and competence in all aspects of Design and Technology.
A key part of the engineering process is evaluation. Children learn to reflect on their ideas, adapt their designs and improve their products — an essential life skill that supports resilience, critical thinking and independence.
We encourage pupils to draw on knowledge and skills from across the curriculum, particularly Maths, Science and Art, helping them see how engineering connects to the wider world.
Engineering Through Enquiry
Some enquiries have being an Engineer as the lead state of being, while many others use engineering as a secondary state. This is because engineering is often the vehicle through which pupils can express and apply their learning in other subjects.
Our enquiries cover the full breadth of the Design and Technology curriculum, including:
Cooking and nutrition
Structures and mechanisms
Textiles and materials
Across all year groups, teaching follows the design → make → evaluate cycle. This ensures pupils develop a clear understanding of the engineering process and can apply it confidently and creatively.

pageCache.pageTitle: Alderbury and West Grimstead Church of England Primary School - Geographer
pageCache.text:
Geographer
Geography at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
Our Being a Geographer curriculum is designed to nurture children’s curiosity, fascination and sense of wonder about the world and its people — a curiosity we hope will stay with them for life.
Through rich, enquiry‑led learning, pupils investigate a wide range of places, both within Britain and across the wider world. This helps them develop a secure understanding of the Earth’s physical and human processes and how these shape the environments we live in.
Learning About Our Local Area
We are committed to helping children develop a strong sense of identity and place. Pupils explore and investigate our local area of Salisbury and Wiltshire, learning about:
Local landmarks and landscapes
Human and physical features
How our community has developed over time
What makes our area unique and special
This grounding in local geography helps children build meaningful connections before exploring the wider world.
Developing Geographical Skills
Throughout their time at AWGS, pupils learn to apply a wide range of geographical skills so they can confidently communicate their findings and understanding. These include:
Map reading and interpretation
Fieldwork techniques
Observing, measuring and recording
Analysing patterns and relationships
Presenting information clearly to different audiences
Essential Characteristics of a Geographer
Through high‑quality teaching, we aim to develop pupils who demonstrate:
Excellent knowledge of where places are and what they are like, in Britain and globally
A deep understanding of how places are interconnected and interdependent
A rich geographical vocabulary and strong subject knowledge
Fluency in enquiry, including questioning, investigating and presenting findings
The ability to draw conclusions and explain their reasoning
Strong fieldwork skills and confidence using geographical tools
Well‑balanced opinions about environmental and societal issues
A genuine interest in the world and the people who live in it

pageCache.pageTitle: Alderbury and West Grimstead Church of England Primary School - Historian
pageCache.text:
Historian
History at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
Being a Historian is taught as part of our Curious City Curriculum, where children learn through rich, enquiry‑led experiences. Each year, pupils explore several enquiries where History is either the lead state of being or a supporting one. This approach helps children understand the past in meaningful, connected ways.
At AWGS, the teaching and learning of History focuses on enabling children to think as historians. Our curriculum is built on the National Curriculum programmes of study for Key Stages 1 and 2 and is structured around three core strands:
Chronological Understanding
Knowledge & Interpretation
What We Teach Historians to Do
Throughout their time at AWGS, pupils learn how to:
Sequence events chronologically using dates and key periods
Ask and answer questions to explore historical concepts
Interpret events and understand that different versions of the same event may exist
Identify continuity and change to understand how the world has developed
Recognise causes of significant events and their consequences
Compare similarities and differences across periods and relate them to their own lives
Understand the significance of key events and their impact on the world
These skills help children develop a deep, reflective understanding of the past and how it shapes the present.
How We Bring History to Life
We provide a wide range of learning experiences to help children think, question and investigate like historians. These include:
Educational visits in the local area and further afield
Handling artefacts to explore different periods and cultures
Using high‑quality resources to bring abstract concepts (e.g. Stone Age, Romans, Mayans) to life
Linking learning to the wider community, helping pupils make meaningful connections
Working with primary and secondary sources to develop critical thinking and interpretation skills

pageCache.pageTitle: Alderbury and West Grimstead Church of England Primary School - Mathematician
pageCache.text:
Mathematician
Maths at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
Mathematics at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
At Alderbury and West Grimstead School, all children will become resilient, fluent mathematicians with an ability to tackle problem solving.
At AWGS, we aim to inspire every pupil to develop a love of Mathematics by providing them with the knowledge, skills and confidence they need to be successful. Our curriculum is designed to build secure understanding, encourage curiosity and enable children to apply their learning to real‑life situations.
Our Maths Curriculum
We follow the White Rose Maths curriculum, which provides a clear, progressive structure from Early Years to Year 6. Concepts are taught in carefully planned blocks, allowing children the time they need to master key ideas before moving on. This approach ensures:
Deep, secure understanding
Regular revisiting of key concepts
Opportunities to apply learning in a range of contexts
Strong foundations for future mathematical learning
You can view the full year overview for your child’s year group by clicking this link.
Our Approach to Teaching Mathematics
We offer pupils a rich, varied and enjoyable experience as mathematicians. Our teaching reflects the three main aims of the National Curriculum:
1. Fluency
Children develop rapid and accurate recall of number facts and methods, enabling them to work confidently and efficiently.
2. Reasoning
Pupils learn to explain their thinking, justify their answers and use mathematical vocabulary with increasing precision.
3. Problem Solving
Children apply their knowledge to a wide range of problems, make connections between concepts, and explore different strategies.
Mathematics in Early Years
In Early Years, Mathematics focuses on:
Counting and ordering numbers to 20
Understanding one more and one less
Early addition and subtraction using practical resources
Doubling, halving and sharing
Exploring shapes and patterns
Using everyday language to describe size, weight, capacity, position, time and money
Children learn through hands‑on exploration, play and meaningful real‑world experiences.
Mathematics in Key Stage 1
In KS1, pupils build confidence with:
Number and place value
Addition and subtraction
Multiplication and division
Shape, space and measure
Using mathematical vocabulary to explain their thinking
Learning is practical and supported by concrete resources and pictorial representations. This provides a strong foundation for the more abstract concepts introduced in Key Stage 2. Children also experience regular Number Sense lessons to secure factual fluency.
Mathematics in Key Stage 2
In KS2, pupils deepen their understanding through:
More complex calculations
Fractions, decimals and percentages
Ratio and proportion
Accurate use of measuring instruments
Applying knowledge to multi‑step problems
Children continue to develop fluency, precision and confidence, including secure recall of multiplication tables up to 12 × 12, which are assessed as part of the national Year 4 Multiplication Times Table Check.
Supporting Maths at Home
We encourage families to explore the White Rose Parent Resources, which include videos, guidance and downloadable materials to support learning at home.

Phonics
Phonics at Alderbury & West Grimstead CE Primary School
At AWGS, we aim to develop confident, fluent readers who foster a genuine love of books from the very start of their learning journey. Early reading is at the heart of our curriculum and high‑quality phonics teaching underpins everything we do.
Our Phonics Programme: Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised
We teach phonics using Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised, a systematic and highly effective programme that supports children to become secure, successful readers.
Families can access a wide range of helpful resources, including pronunciation guides, phoneme finders and progression documents, directly from the Little Wandle website. These materials are ideal for supporting phonics learning at home.
Our Reading Books: Collins Big Cat
To complement our phonics teaching, we use Collins Big Cat fully‑decodable books. These are carefully matched to each child’s phonics stage so they can practise the sounds they have learned in school with confidence and success.
